author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected afterwards. The correction form opens prefilled with the visit's current date and description, is judged by the booking rules, and replaces that visit in place.
acceptance_criteria: Given a booked visit, when its correction page is opened, then the visit form is shown carrying that visit's current date and description.
Given a correction with a description and a date later than today, when it is submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown.
Given a pet with one visit, when that visit is corrected, then the pet still has exactly one visit.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the description is named.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the date is named.
Edge case 3: a correction changes only the visit its address names; the pet's other visits keep the dates and descriptions they had.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit — NG-5 still declines it.
Any entry point to the correction page: the owner detail page gains no edit link in this slice.
Correcting anything on a visit other than its date and its description.
notes: Owner decided both product questions at intake (line 1); no further product answer is coming. Two choices were settled by the narrowest reading and recorded as Open Questions in docs/prd.md rather than escalated: (1) a visible entry point stays out until a follow-up request; (2) a correction is validated as a booking is, so a visit whose date has passed cannot be corrected without moving its date. Also outstanding, outside my write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-16-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction reuses the owner aggregate exactly as booking does, with one adjustment to an existing pattern. VisitController's shared @ModelAttribute("visit") method gains an optional visitId branch, the same shape PetController.findPet already uses for its optional petId (PetController.java:75-87, read directly; no IDE oracle connected). On the edit branch it resolves the visit by traversing the single loaded owner to the pet to the visit, and returns that existing instance rather than a new one. Spring MVC then binds the submitted date and description onto the instance already inside pet.getVisits(), which IS the in-place update: no addVisit call, no second record. Persistence stays the documented one: this.owners.save(owner) cascades a merge, and the visit carries an id, so JPA issues an UPDATE (docs/system-design.md Contracts, Invariants the rows cannot carry). The redirect target matches the creation path exactly: both return redirect:/owners/{ownerId}, and both PetController write paths use the same target, so the owner detail page needs no new routing.
integration_points: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit takes @PathVariable(name = "visitId", required = false) Integer visitId; when null it keeps today's behaviour (new Visit, pet.addVisit), when present it returns pet.getVisit(visitId) and adds nothing to the pet.

Pet gains getVisit(Integer id) returning the visit with that identity or null, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer). Keeps aggregate traversal in the model rather than adding a stream filter to the controller.

Two new handlers on the existing routes: initUpdateVisitForm on GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit returning pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, and processUpdateVisitForm on POST to the same URL, mirroring PetController.initUpdateForm/processUpdateForm naming.

processUpdateVisitForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner and @Valid Visit visit, applies the same non-future-date rejection, and on success calls this.owners.save(owner) then returns redirect:/owners/{ownerId} — identical to processNewVisitForm.

No template change is required: the form carries no th:action, so it posts to the current URL, and ${visit['new']} already renders the non-new case (heading without the New prefix, previous-visits table populated).

patterns.description: one @ModelAttribute method serving both create and edit via an optional @PathVariable — the pattern the visit model attribute adopts
getPet(Integer) aggregate-navigation accessor returning null when absent — the shape Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors
the booking handler whose validation, save-through-owner, and redirect target the correction handler repeats

risks.risk: The edit branch reuses loadPetWithVisit's pet.addVisit(visit) call and the pet gains a second visit, breaking the in-place criterion.
risks.mitigation: Branch before the construction: the visitId-present path returns the existing instance only. The test asserting the pet still holds exactly one visit is the guard.

risks.risk: Duplicating the non-future-date check into the second handler adds a fresh controller-held business rule, which architecture-principles.md line 91 forbids even though the existing check is a recorded deviation.
risks.mitigation: Extract the existing check in processNewVisitForm into one private method in VisitController and call it from both handlers. One rule, one place, two surfaces. Do not move it to a Validator or a bean-validation annotation in this slice: that changes the typeMismatch.visitDate code REQ-VIS-001 tests assert on.

risks.risk: A visitId naming a visit that belongs to another pet or owner would let a caller correct a record the URL does not own — the path variables are the untrusted input here (docs/security-principles.md trust boundaries).
risks.mitigation: Resolve strictly by traversal from the loaded owner; there is no VisitRepository, so no global lookup exists. When pet.getVisit(visitId) returns null, throw IllegalArgumentException as the missing-pet branch above it already does. This also delivers PRD edge case 3.

risks.risk: A failed correction leaves the mutated visit in the aggregate and could reach the database.
risks.mitigation: None needed: spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled and findById runs in its own transaction, so the owner graph is detached and only an explicit owners.save writes. The error path returns the view without saving.

notes:
Narrow readings recorded, per the owner's instruction that no further product answer is coming. (1) No flash message on the correction path: no acceptance criterion asks for one, and both existing flash strings are hard-coded English literals in controllers, which REQ-LANG-002 already counts against the codebase — a third literal extends a known breach. (2) No template change and no new message key: the submit button keeps #{addVisit}. A correction-specific label needs a new key in all eleven bundles, which I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces, and no criterion asks for it. Copying createOrUpdatePetForm.html's hard-coded 'Add Pet' : 'Update Pet' ternary would extend the same REQ-LANG-002 breach.
Use owners.save(owner), not saveAndFlush. saveAndFlush exists in PetController only because it needs the integrity violation eagerly for duplicate pet names; the visit path has no such constraint.
Test shape: the @MockitoBean OwnerRepository fixture returns one Owner instance, and binding mutates that instance. Hold a reference to the fixture owner in the test and assert on pet.getVisits() directly — size unchanged, date and description updated. No ArgumentCaptor is needed, which keeps the new tests within CLAUDE.md's minimal-mocking rule. The fixture needs a Visit with an id set for the edit tests.
docs/ writes made with this triage: docs/system-design.md Contracts rows for Owner, Pet, Visit, OwnerRepository, and VisitController now carry REQ-VISITEDIT-001, and the Invariants paragraph records that a booked visit is corrected in place through the same cascade. docs/adr/README.md gained the missing index row for 2026-08-16-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md, which the prd-entry flagged as outstanding.
No new ADR. The product decision is already recorded in the 2026-08-16 non-goal ADR, and the implementation choice is the pet-edit shape applied unchanged — a straightforward choice with no trade-off to document.
No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log; the audit step found nothing to judge.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: this change touches no build file (git diff over build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle/ is empty), so it adds no dependency and clears the 'Adding a New Dependency' checks vacuously. Note for the record that no NVD match ran in this review - the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47), and this reviewer has no network access. Spring Boot 4.1.0 is therefore not verified against the NVD here; a human or CI should close that check. The project does publish a CycloneDX SBOM, which is the right hook for it.

Both POST handlers take @ModelAttribute Owner owner and then owners.save(owner), so request parameters matching Owner's non-identifier properties (firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone) bind onto the loaded aggregate and are persisted as a side effect of a visit write. This is pre-existing in processNewVisitForm and the new handler only repeats it on a second route, so it is not a regression against the recorded baseline and identifiers stay disallowed by the @InitBinder. Worth noting anyway because this is a demonstration application that gets copied: a follow-up could narrow the handlers to bind only the visit and re-fetch the owner for the save.

The correction endpoint is state-mutating and, like every other route in this sample, unauthenticated and without CSRF protection - the recorded demonstration baseline (system-design.md Security Context), not a defect of this change. Flagged only so the new mutating route is on the record as part of the exposed surface the PRD and system-design now describe.
approved_aspects: Broken-object-level-authorization (IDOR) is closed by construction on the new routes. VisitController.loadPetWithVisit (VisitController.java:69-96) resolves the visit only by traversing the aggregate loaded from the request's own ownerId: owners.findById(ownerId) then owner.getPet(petId) then pet.getVisit(visitId). There is no VisitRepository and no global lookup, so a visitId naming another pet's or another owner's visit cannot resolve; it falls through to the IllegalArgumentException at VisitController.java:91-94. Verified by direct read of VisitController, Pet, Owner and by grep for 'VisitRepository' across src/main/java (no such type); no IDE oracle is connected, so this is the grep-plus-read basis, not a resolved-symbol basis.

Trusting cross-request state (security-principles.md Realization row) is respected: both new handlers re-resolve owner, pet and visit from the path on every request via the shared @ModelAttribute method. Nothing is carried in session or trusted from the prior GET.

Mass assignment stays closed on the new surface. The class-level @InitBinder at VisitController.java:53-56 applies to every model attribute in this controller, including the new edit binding, and disallows 'id' and '*.id'. A caller therefore cannot rebind Visit.id, Pet.id, or Owner.id through the new POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit route. The identifier the correction acts on comes from the path and is re-resolved, never from a bound field.

Input validation on the correction path is identical to booking's, not a weaker parallel copy: @Valid on the Visit parameter keeps @NotBlank on description (Visit.java:42-43), and the non-future-date rule was extracted into the single private rejectDateNotInFuture (VisitController.java:152-156) called from both handlers. One rule, one implementation - the Pattern Consistency item is met rather than diverged from.

No injection surface is added. Data access remains OwnerRepository derived queries; no string-concatenated query text, no Runtime/ProcessBuilder, no filesystem or classpath resource selection from request-derived values. Greps for 'Runtime|ProcessBuilder|exec(', 'enableDefaultTyping|JsonTypeInfo', and file-I/O patterns return nothing in the changed production files.

XSS: no template changed and no escaping was disabled. src/main/resources/templates/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html renders the now-editable visit values through th:text and the th:field input fragment only; a grep for 'th:utext', 'unescaped', and Thymeleaf preprocessing '__${' across src/main/resources/templates returns no hits. The edit flow renders stored, user-supplied descriptions through the same escaped path booking already used.

Fail-secure on the error path: spring.jpa.open-in-view=false (application.properties:11) means the traversed owner graph is detached, so the visit instance mutated by binding is only persisted by the explicit owners.save(owner). A rejected correction returns the form without saving, leaving no partially-applied write. Confirmed by grep of application.properties plus read of the handler.

No secret, credential, or connection string is added, logged, or placed in an exception message. The new IllegalArgumentException at VisitController.java:92-93 carries only the numeric visitId and petId already present in the request URL, in the same shape as the pre-existing missing-owner and missing-pet messages, so it adds nothing to what the error page already renders.

Given a correction with a description and a date later than today, when it is submitted, then that visit carries the new values and the owner's record is shown.
Given a pet with one visit, when that visit is corrected, then the pet still has exactly one visit.
Given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the description is named.
Given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the date is named.
Edge case 3: a correction changes only the visit its address names; the pet's other visits keep the dates and descriptions they had.
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit — NG-5 still declines it.
Any entry point to the correction page: the owner detail page gains no edit link in this slice.
Correcting anything on a visit other than its date and its description.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The round-1 consistent-with-codebase fix replaced the Hamcrest model().attribute(hasProperty(...)) assertions with model().attributeExists("visit") plus a read of this.pet.getVisit(TEST_VISIT_ID).getDate()/getDescription(). This is a regression, not a like-for-like rewrite: the GET handler (VisitController.initUpdateVisitForm, via the shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loadPetWithVisit) performs no data binding on a GET, so the model's "visit" attribute is always the exact same object instance as this.pet.getVisit(TEST_VISIT_ID) -- untouched by the request. The new assertions therefore read back the test's own fixture data, not anything the controller placed in the model; they pass unconditionally regardless of what loadPetWithVisit actually returns (a wrong visit, an empty new Visit(), or nothing). The test's name (theVisitCorrectionFormShouldShowTheCurrentDateAndDescription) and PRD acceptance criterion 1 ("the visit form is shown carrying that visit's current date and description") are no longer verified by this test's body -- it is now vacuous for the one behavior it claims to specify. The sibling POST-side tests this fix was made consistent with (theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlace) are not vacuous in the same way, because POST does bind submitted values onto the same pet-held instance, so reading it back afterward reflects real mutation; that reasoning does not carry over to a read-only GET.
findings.fix: Capture the MvcResult and assert on the actual model attribute the controller returned, e.g.: `MvcResult result = mockMvc.perform(get(...)).andExpect(status().isOk()).andExpect(view().name("pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm")).andReturn(); Visit shown = (Visit) result.getModelAndView().getModel().get("visit"); assertThat(shown.getDate()).isEqualTo(BOOKED_DATE); assertThat(shown.getDescription()).isEqualTo(BOOKED_DESCRIPTION);` This keeps the fluent AssertJ style the rest of the class uses while actually exercising the GET handler's model content instead of the untouched fixture.

approved_aspects: Both round-1 findings' mechanical intent is otherwise satisfied: a createVisit(int, LocalDate, String) factory now backs both the init() booked-visit construction and the other-visit construction in theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveThePetsOtherVisitsUntouched, and the unused Hamcrest static imports were removed.
docs/prd.md:189 is out of this reviewer's scope (doc-reviewer's finding) and reads correctly on inspection.

All other tests in the fix-delta (theVisitCorrectionShouldUpdateTheVisitInPlace, theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveThePetsVisitCountUnchanged, theVisitCorrectionShouldLeaveThePetsOtherVisitsUntouched, the two refusal tests) correctly assert on state that the exercised request path actually mutates or produces, and remain sound.
